methods.name: BRICS+SAFE
methods.training: BRICS uses fixed fragmentation rules. The existing SAFE text vocabulary is loaded; it is not retrained in this experiment.
methods.decode: Text IDs → complete SAFE string → SMILES. Connectivity is recovered from the SAFE string.

code.train:
TRAIN(training_SAFE_strings, vocabulary_size):
    use predefined BRICS fragmentation rules
    learn a SAFE text-token vocabulary from training strings
    return text_tokenizer

# This experiment loads an existing text tokenizer.
# Its original training corpus has not been verified.
code.encode:
ENCODE(smiles, text_tokenizer):
    safe = SAFE.encode(smiles, slicer=BRICS)
    ids = text_tokenizer.encode(safe,
        add_special_tokens=False, padding=False,
        truncation=False, dropout=0)
    return safe, ids, len(ids)

methods.name: Original DemoDiff
methods.training: NPE/GraphBPE learns graph motifs through frequent adjacent-subgraph merges. This experiment loads the existing pretrain-token vocabulary: 3,000 node entries and 300 ring entries.
methods.decode: Node IDs + bond adjacency + attachment positions → SMILES. Node IDs alone do not specify connectivity.

code.train:
TRAIN(training_molecular_graphs, target_size):
    initialize graph vocabulary and ring handling
    repeat until target_size or no eligible merge:
        count eligible adjacent-subgraph pairs
        merge the most frequent pair in training graphs
        add the resulting motif to the node vocabulary
    retain node, ring and edge/attachment vocabularies

# Conceptual NPE training, not rerun for this experiment.
# The original vocabulary training corpus is unverified.
code.encode:
ENCODE(original_smiles, tokenizer):
    node_ids, adj = tokenizer.encode(
        original_smiles, update_vocab_edge=False)
    bonds, positions = tokenizer.get_bond_position_by_vocab(adj)
    return node_ids, bonds, positions, len(node_ids)

methods.decode: Complete SAFE string → SMILES. The current motif-ID mapping is not a standalone reversible model-token sequence.

code.encode:
ENCODE_AND_AUDIT(smiles, vocabulary):
    # SAFE calls BPESlicer on its own working molecule.
    # Expanded implementation: Step 1 below.
    record = encode_graphbpe_safe(smiles, vocabulary)

    # Cohort selection is a separate analysis step.
    # Boundary changes are not automatically decoding failures.
    # Expanded selection rules: Step 2 below.

    # Optional fixed-boundary lookup: no second GraphBPE pass.
    # Expanded atom tracking and extraction: Step 3 below.
    mapping = map_fixed_SAFE_fragments(record.safe, vocabulary)
    # Unknown motif keys are reported; they are not resegmented.
    return record, mapping

# Reported aggregate counts reuse len(record.bpe_node_ids)
# AFTER exact-boundary validation. Examples also verify mapping.
# Full SAFE retains connectivity; motif IDs alone are not reversible.
# Names above describe pseudocode, not new public APIs.
code.decode:
DECODE(safe, motif_ids):
    # Parse the COMPLETE SAFE string with matched labels.
    # A label identifies a pair, not an atom index or token ID.
    mol = parse_complete_SAFE(safe, repair_missing_labels=False)
    return write_canonical_isomeric_SMILES(mol)

# Example: CC1.O1 -> CCO
# Matching "1" labels connect the second C to O.
# Dots separate fragments; labels, their atom positions,
# and bond syntax carry connectivity.
# motif_ids are not used to reconstruct the molecule.
# Decoding from motif_ids alone is not implemented.

limitations: Motif/node counts exclude connectivity overhead; SAFE text counts include it. Their ratio is not a full-encoding compression ratio.
SAFE dots separate fragments. Paired labels, their attachment positions and bond symbols carry cross-fragment connectivity; dots alone do not specify bonds.
The three examples pass molecular round-trip checks. Successful encoding of the full DemoDiff batch does not establish lossless reconstruction for every molecule.
This evaluation loads existing vocabularies. It does not establish that those vocabularies were trained on these 50,000 molecules.

graph_encode_details.title: 1. SAFE serialization: proposed cuts → paired labels
graph_encode_details.description: Actual path: SAFEConverter.encoder invokes BPESlicer on the converter's working molecule. The slicer tracks atom reordering, proposes cross-group bonds, and records GraphBPE groups and IDs. The pseudocode below describes the closed-molecule experiment with no additional constraints and ignore_stereo=False.
graph_encode_details.code:
ENCODE_GRAPHBPE_SAFE(smiles, vocabulary):
    mol = parse_and_normalize(smiles)
    original_mol = copy(mol)
    original_SMILES = write_isomeric_SMILES(mol)
    groups, motif_ids = BPESlicer.partition_with_atom_tracking(
        mol, vocabulary)
    owner[atom] = its GraphBPE group

    requested_cuts = [
        bond(u, v) for bond(u, v) in mol
        if owner[u] != owner[v]
    ]
    used_cuts = current_stereo_filter(mol, requested_cuts)
    safe_groups = connected_components(
        copy(mol) with used_cuts removed)

    # Aromatic cuts use the slicer's Kekule convention.
    prepare_aromatic_bonds_if_required(mol, used_cuts)
    fragmented = FragmentOnBonds(
        mol, used_cuts,
        dummyLabels=[(k, k) for k in 1..number_of_cuts])
    # Both ends of the same cut receive the same dummy label.

    fragments = sort_by_size(get_fragments(fragmented))
    text = join(write_isomeric_SMILES(f) for f in fragments, ".")
    label = 1 + max_ring_label(original_SMILES, text, default=0)

    for dummy_marker in sorted_distinct_dummy_markers(text):
        replace both occurrences with format_ring_label(label)
        label += 1
    safe = normalize_ring_closure_syntax(text)

    # The converter can return the intact input if its final
    # specified-stereochemistry check detects a change.
    safe = apply_converter_identity_guard(safe, original_mol)
    require dot_fragment_count(safe) == len(safe_groups)
    require isomeric_identity(parse(safe)) == isomeric_identity(original_mol)

    return {safe, groups, safe_groups, motif_ids,
            requested_cuts, used_cuts}
graph_encode_details.notes: The current stereo filter is more conservative than simply forbidding stereogenic double-bond cuts: some single bonds and non-single bonds in molecules with specified E/Z information are also protected. This describes the current project implementation, not a universal ban on those bond types. Dummy atoms are temporary construction markers, not extra atoms in the reconstructed closed molecule.

graph_encode_details.title: 2. Boundary-preserving comparison: audit first, select separately
graph_encode_details.description: The batch pipeline records requested versus accepted cut sets. AuditedConverter derives safe_groups by removing accepted cuts from a copy of the working graph, not by taking connected components after parsing the complete SAFE string.
graph_encode_details.code:
SELECT_EXACT_RECORDS(records):
    selected = []
    for r in records:
        # Unordered atom pairs; endpoint ordering is irrelevant.
        exact = undirected_set(r.requested_cuts) == (
                undirected_set(r.used_cuts))
        require exact == r.bpe_boundary_exact

        if not exact:
            count_as_boundary_changed()
            continue  # Excluded from this comparison only.

        require normalize_partition(r.bpe_groups) == (
                normalize_partition(r.safe_groups))
        require len(r.bpe_node_ids) == len(r.bpe_groups) == (
                len(r.safe_groups)) == dot_fragment_count(r.safe)
        require len(r.bpe_node_ids) == r.num_bpe_fragments == (
                r.num_safe_fragments)
        require r.roundtrip_ok is True

        selected.append(r)
    return selected

NORMALIZE_PARTITION(groups):
    return sort(sort(atom_indices) for atom_indices in groups)

# Pipeline.convert records the cut-set comparison.
# export_exact_graphbpe.py consumes that flag and additionally
# validates partitions, counts, IDs and the round-trip flag.
# Equal fragment counts alone do not establish equal boundaries.
graph_encode_details.notes: Strict batch mode rejects boundary changes. With --allow-stereo-coarsening, successful changed-boundary records can be saved and excluded later from the exact-boundary comparison. The existing outputs contain 49,992 successful records: 5,663 changed boundaries, 44,329 exact boundaries, and 44,328 exact records shared with BRICS. Audit cut lists are not required as inputs to SAFE decoding.

graph_encode_details.title: 3. Fixed fragment lookup: complete graph → owner-tracked subgraphs
graph_encode_details.description: Parse the complete SAFE string so every connection label can be resolved. Separately scan atom lexemes to remember which dot-separated fragment contributed each atom; bracket atoms and Cl/Br each count as one atom.
graph_encode_details.code:
MAP_FIXED_SAFE_FRAGMENTS(safe, tokenizer):
    fragments = split(safe, ".")
    mol = parse_complete_SAFE(safe, removeHs=False)
    # Reject unsupported syntax, atom maps and dummy atoms.

    owners = []
    fragment_id = 0
    for lexeme in scan_SMILES_lexemes(safe):
        if lexeme == ".":
            fragment_id += 1
        else if is_atom(lexeme):
            owners.append(fragment_id)
    require len(owners) == mol.number_of_atoms

    # Each canonical write/reparse can reorder atoms.
    # Use RDKit _smilesAtomOutputOrder to reorder owners too.
    mol, owners = match_DemoDiff_preprocessing_with_tracking(
        mol, owners, tokenizer.kekulize)

    ids = []
    for f in range(len(fragments)):
        atoms = [i for i in mol.atoms if owners[i] == f]
        submol = upstream.get_sub_molecule(
            mol, atoms, kekulize=tokenizer.kekulize)
        require submol.number_of_atoms == len(atoms)
        key = upstream_compatible_motif_key(submol)

        if key not in tokenizer.node_vocabulary:
            report_missing_key(fragments[f], key)
            # Strict mode raises; diagnostic mode returns None.
            # Never rerun GraphBPE to force a vocabulary match.
        ids.append(lookup_or_None(key))

    return {safe, ids, coverage, ids_are_lossless: False}

# CC1.O1: atom lexemes = [C, C, O]; owners = [0, 0, 1].
# Extract internal bonds for group 0 and the single atom for group 1.
# CC1 and O1 cannot be parsed independently as complete molecules.
graph_encode_details.notes: The adapter reuses DemoDiff's key convention, including its single-atom helper, which reconstructs from the element symbol. A vocabulary key is therefore not a lossless copy of all chemical attributes. Mapping IDs follow SAFE fragment order; recorded bpe_node_ids follow GraphBPE group order. Full SAFE remains necessary for reconstruction.
